title: Determinants of gambling behavior among out-of-school adolescents in the Ibadan metropolis, Oyo state, Nigeria
abstract: Gambling is an activity that occupies different spaces and roles across different cultures. Gambling do not only lead to waste of resources but could also lead to depression, anxiety, restlessness, suicidal thought or suicide. While much has been written about gambling in developed nation, only few studies have examined the predictive factor of gambling among out of school adolescents in Nigeria. This study, therefore investigated dysfunctional family, socio economic status and religiosity as determinants of gambling among out-of-school adolescents in the Ibadan Metropolis. A descriptive research design of correlational type was employed in the selection of Two hundred and fifty (250) out-of-school adolescents within the Ibadan Metropolis using simple random sampling technique. Three research questions were raised and answered in the study. The independent variables were measured with relevant standardized instruments. These include dysfunctional family scale (α =.68) socio economic status (α = .64) religiosity (α= .73) and the gambling motivation scale (r = .69). title: “From vulnerability to violence”: sexual victimization as a challenge faced by street children. A case study of urban district Zanzibar
abstract: The study aimed at exploring sexual victimization as a challenge faced by street children. To get clear understanding of the study, different literature was consulted, including sociological study to help in understanding street children, child protection and abuse literature to understand violence and abuse, human rights and legal literature to highlight child right and final Routine Activity Theory which explains why crimes happen in everyday life. The study employed qualitative approach in which 30 participants were obtained through purposive sampling and snowball technique. Data collection methods included focused group discussion, in depth interview and documentary review. Data were analysis through thematic analysis procedures. NVIVO version 16 was used to analyze data obtained from the field. The finding revealed different form of sexual victimization faced by street children including rape, transectional sex, commercial sex and sexual harassment. On the other hand the study explored the nature of commercial sex among street children including coercive commercial sex and survival based commercial sex. title: Media literacy education and development of children, adolescents and young adults in Nigeria
abstract: The media, including print, broadcast, social, and other online sources, are core features of the present digital society. Media literacy is concerned with a set of skills and competencies required to access, analyse, evaluate, create, understand and use the complex messages communicated via all forms of media. Our children, adolescents, and young adults (CAYA) are constantly exposed to a variety of media, with their content and messages, many of which are uncivil and alien to our culture, values and norms. Unfortunately, the educational system of Nigeria, specifically at the primary, secondary, and tertiary school levels, did not make provisions for inculcating media literacy skills in these CAYA for understanding, withstanding, and appropriately coping with the messages of these media outlets. This is in addition to scholarly publications that revealed obvious loopholes with reference to media literacy skills level of CAYA in the society. Thus, there is a media literacy gap that needs to be addressed. This paper articulated the concept of media literacy, media literacy education, developing media literacy skills using appropriate learning theories, and strategies of fostering and

title: Maintenance of standard as bases for quality: an evaluation of pre-NCE programme of college of education obudu, cross river state, Nigeria.
abstract: The study was designed to evaluate the pre-NCE programme of the College of Education Obudu in terms of respecting the National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE) standard for operation. Detail literature review was carried out on the variables of the study while ex-post facto research design was adopted and census sampling approach was used by this the entire enrolment of 4114 in 2019/2020, 2020/2021, and 2021/2022 was used. The instrument used for data collection was interview. The data collected for analysis was students records which include their enrolment list, their performance at internal/external examination and list of transited students, Simple percentage and ratio was used to analyses the data. The results revealed that the College did not respect either transition requirement to NCE programme nor respect the nation benchmark of admission of 30:70 ratio for Art and Science based courses. Based on the findings, it was recommended that NCCE should monitor Colleges well to see that they keep all standard expected of them in order to improve the quality of their graduates that will turn out teachers for our basic school in Nigeria.

title: Collaborative strategies for the effective application of artificial intelligence in teaching of business education courses in tertiary institutions in cross river state
abstract: The effective application of AI in teaching Business Education courses in tertiary institutions is fraught with challenges that necessitate collaborative strategies among stakeholders. This study ascertained the collaborative strategies for the effective application of Artificial Intelligence in teaching of Business Education courses in tertiary institutions in Cross River State. Two specific purposes and research questions guided the study. Descriptive research design was used in the study. The population comprised 96 business educators in four public tertiary institutions in Cross River State. The population size was manageable, therefore census sampling technique was adopted. The instruments used for data collection was questionnaire of four rating scale designed by the researcher. The instruments was validated by three experts and tested for reliability using Cronbach Alpha coefficient. The overall reliability obtained was 0.83. Data collected were tested in SPSS using mean and standard deviation to answer the research questions. Findings revealed that interdisciplinary team formation, co-design with stakeholders, cross-institutional research networks, industry-academia partner

title: Context matters: assessment and feedback in rural and urban junior high school English language classrooms in Ghana
abstract: This multiple-case qualitative study explored how English teachers in rural and urban Junior High Schools in Ho Municipality, Ghana, assess learners and provide feedback in classrooms where digital technologies were unavailable or unusable. Six English teachers (three rural; three urban) were selected through criterion-based purposive sampling. Data were generated through semi-structured interviews, classroom observations, and document analysis of learners' exercise books. Instruments were refined through expert review and piloting and the dataset was analysed thematically with cross-case comparison. Findings indicate that teachers in both settings relied mainly on oral questioning and short written tasks for formative purposes, alongside periodic tests for summative purposes. However, feedback was predominantly evaluative and corrective with limited opportunity for learner uptake through revision. Urban cases showed more structured marking while rural cases more often faced non-specialist teaching and acute resource constraints that narrowed feedback options. Conceptually, the study characterises these patterns as analogue feedback ecologies where teacher specialism and class size

title: Demographic factors and the dissemination of misinformation on social media among undergraduate students in university of Calabar, cross river state, Nigeria
abstract: The study examined demographic factors and the dissemination of misinformation on social media among undergraduate students in University of Calabar. Two purposes and two research questions were formulated. The study adopted the descriptive survey research design, with a sample of 256 undergraduate students from the department of Mass Communication, University of Calabar for the 2023/2024 academic session. The major instrument used for data collection was Social Media Use and Fake News Dissemination Questionnaire (SMUFNDQ). Data collection was done by the researcher who randomly administered the instruments to the students. The data collected were analyzed using frequency counts and the results of the analysis revealed that over 50% of the respondents have a negative perception of fake news dissemination. Also there was a significant relationship between social media and fake news dissemination among the students’. It was also revealed that the probability of sharing misinformation on social media was higher among female students, and students between the ages of 26-30 years. title: Ethical personnel management practices and institutional goal attainment in public secondary schools: evidence from Calabar municipality, cross river state - Nigeria
abstract: This study investigated the relationship between ethical personnel management practices and institutional goal attainment in public secondary schools in Calabar Municipality, Cross River State, Nigeria. Guided by Goal Setting Theory and Herzberg’s Two-Factor Theory, the study examined three dimensions of ethical personnel management, namely: management–staff relations, employee promotion, and financial benefits and their relationships with school goal attainment. A correlational research design was adopted, with data collected from 155 teachers out of a population of 473 using systematic random sampling technique. Data were generated through questionnaire titled, “Personnel Management Practices and Goal Attainment of Secondary Schools Questionnaire (PMPGASSQ)”, which was validated by three experts, and reliabilited tested with a reliability coefficient of .87 using Crobach Alpha reliability analysis. Data analysis involved weighted means, standard deviations, and Pearson Product Moment Correlation at the 0.05 significance level. Findings revealed that management–staff relations (r = 0.656), employee promotion (r = 0.674), and employee financial benefits (r = 0.750) positively and s

title: Management of content development studio and smart schools’ sustainability in south-south Nigeria
abstract: The digitization of basic education in developing economies requires structural frameworks that guarantee infrastructural longevity. This study investigated the relationship between the management of content development studios and smart school sustainability in South-South Nigeria. Grounded in the Resource-Based View (RBV) theory, the study conceptualizes studio management through three dimensions: studio infrastructure maintenance, digital content quality control, and technical staff capacity building. A descriptive survey design was adopted, utilizing a census sampling approach that targeted the entire population of principals, Information and Communication Technology (ICT) coordinators, and studio managers (N = 108) across pilot smart schools in the region. Data collection was executed using a structured 5-point Likert scale instrument titled "Management of Content Studios and Smart School Sustainability Questionnaire" (MCSSSSQ). Research questions are analyzed using Mean {x̄} and Standard Deviation (SD) against a criterion threshold of 2.50, while only one hypothesis was ested using and Multiple Linear Regression at 0.05 level of significance. title: Leveraging artificial intelligence (ai) for job creation in emerging economies: evidence from Nigeria’s technology and education sector
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a set of technologies that enable computers to perform a variety of advanced functions, including the ability to see, understand and translate spoken and written language, analyze data, make recommendations, and many more. It is often assumed that artificial intelligence would eliminate jobs and raise unemployment. The same was assumed when the Internet was in its early stages, but the internet opened far more new doors and provided individuals with new work prospects that no one could have imagined at the time. With the progress of Artificial Intelligence, we can say the same thing is possible. This paper shall examines the concepts of artificial intelligence and the place of job creation, it shall discuss the relevance of job creation and AI perspectives, examine criticism from different scholar regarding the two concepts and the role of artificial intelligence and job creation will be mention which are; skill transformation, job displacement, debate, organizational productivity, entrepreneurship development in generating new employment opportunities, while enhancing productivity. title: Self-awareness and attitudes of public-school teachers towards family planning in delta and Edo states, Nigeria
abstract: The extent to which one is informed about the practice and benefits of family planning influences one’s decisions and levels of acceptance of the practices. This study examined how the levels of awareness of public school teachers influence their attitudes towards the practice of family planning in Delta and Edo States. Correlational survey design was adopted in this study. The population was 20,038 public school teachers, from which 2,003 being 10% of the study population was sampled. The population of 1,242 and 761 which represented 10% of public school teachers in the 463 and 259 public schools in Delta and Edo States respectively were selected using the stratified proportional random technique of sampling. This research investigation was carried out in 722 public secondary schools. The study made use of questionnaire as research instrument for the collection of data for a period of one month which involved the services of field assistants. The instrument’s reliability and coefficient Alpha were ascertained following Cronbach's Alpha statistics. The values of the internal constancy dependability for self-awareness scale was 0.86 (P

title: Psychological variables and research skills acquisition among postgraduate students in public universities in cross river state, Nigeria
abstract: This study assessed psychological variables and research skills acquisition among postgraduate students in public universities in Cross River State, Nigeria. Ex post factor research design was adopted for the study, while stratified random sampling technique was used to select a sample of 400 from a population of 2,651 post graduate students in the universities of the study. An instrument developed by the researcher and titled: “Research Skills Acquisition Questionnaire” (PVRSAQ), duly validated with reliability estimates of the sub-variables between .72 and .81 was used to collect data for the study. The data collected were subjected to statistical analysis using simple linear regression analysis. The study revealed that psychological variables (attitude to; and, interest in research methods) significantly influence the postgraduate’s education students’ research skills acquisition. Based on the findings, it was recommended among others, that educators should consider focusing on developing intervention aimed at improving students’ attitudes towards research and identifying best practices for enhancing research engagements in postgraduate education. Also, educators are encouraged

title: Co-curricular and extracurricular ICT activities, assessment practices, and female students’ interest in ICT-related pathways in Ghana
abstract: Across many education systems, expanding access to information and communication technology (ICT) education forms part of national development agendas, yet women remain underrepresented in ICT pathways. Guided by Expectancy-Value Theory and the Leaky Pipeline metaphor, this mixed-methods study examined how co-curricular and extracurricular ICT activities and assessment practices were associated with first-year female students’ interest in ICT-related programmes in higher education. Survey data were collected from 410 female Level 100 students in a public university in Ghana, followed by interviews with 11 participants reflecting retrospectively on their Senior High School ICT experiences. Simple regression analyses showed that both co-curricular and extracurricular ICT activities and assessment practices significantly predicted interest, with assessment practices explaining more variance. In the simultaneous model, however, only assessment practices made a significant unique contribution, while co-curricular and extracurricular ICT activities were not significant. title: Resource availability, students’ perceived quality, and functionality of school health centers in selected south-south Nigerian states: a public–private comparative study
abstract: Background: School health centres are expected to provide accessible, safe, and responsive care for learners during school hours, yet implementation in Nigeria remains uneven despite policy provisions for school health services. This study assessed resource availability, students' perceived quality, and the functionality of school health centres in selected South-South Nigerian states. Methodology: A comparative cross-sectional baseline assessment was conducted between March and June 2012 across 30 secondary schools in three South-South Nigerian states, with five public and five private schools selected per state capital. The analytic sample comprised 2,843 senior secondary students and 31 school health-centre managers or responsible officers. Data were collected using structured questionnaires and a structural checklist. Public-private differences were examined using chi-square tests and crude binary logistic odds ratios at p

title: Diversity of business education courses and academic achievement of undergraduates in university of Calabar - Nigeria
abstract: This study determined how preferences for specialised areas of business education - accounting, entrepreneurship, office management, and marketing and distributive education predict the academic achievement of business education students in University of Calabar using results of four different courses as determinant factors. The study answered four research questions and tested four null hypotheses. The study adopted a descriptive survey design and was conducted in Calabar. The population of the study comprised 96 participants, including 32 business education lecturers and 64 students who completed year one under the CCMAS curriculum. The purposive sampling technique enabled the use of all 96 respondents. Data were collected using a researcher-designed questionnaire, the "Diversity of Business Education Courses and Academic Achievement of Undergraduates Questionnaire (DBECAAQ)," validated by three experts. Simple linear regression was used for data analysis. The findings reveal that accounting, entrepreneurship, office management, and marketing and distributive education significantly predict academic achievement of business education students. title: Enhancing access to and participation in education for day students in Tanzanian secondary schools: trends, major challenges, and remedies
abstract: This study investigated the trends, major challenges, and potential remedies concerning access to and participation in education for day students in secondary schools in Tanzania. The study population consisted of Kibasila and Jangwani secondary schools in Dar es Salaam, from which 100 students and 30 teachers were selected through stratified and cluster sampling. Qualitative and quantitative designs were adopted. Questionnaires were administered to teachers and students. In addition, a focus group discussion with students was employed in order to get information on access and participation challenges and their possible remedies. Data was analyzed qualitatively and quantitatively using descriptive statistics and the Kruskal - Walli’s test. The findings show that enrolment was rising and retention was falling, despite the students many challenges. The study revealed that student attendance was poor. The study also showed that distance had an impact only on attendance, while time had an impact on enrolment, attendance, and retention trends. The major challenges identified include transport, distance from home to school, and financial constraints. Measures proposed to minimize or alle

title: Drama in health education: a tool for sensitization of menstrual cramps among students in secondary schools: a case study of government girls’ secondary school, big qua town Calabar, Calabar municipality of cross river state Nigeria
abstract: This study explores the effectiveness of Drama in health education as a tool for sensitizing teenage girls about menstrual cramps using Big qua girls’ Secondary school as a case study. Grounded in Albert Banduras social learning theory, the research employed an experimental design with 120 participants divided equally into an experimental group engaged in drama based menstrual health education sessions while the control group received traditional classroom instructions. Pre-test and post-test questionnaire assessed participant’s menstrual cramps. The results from this study revealed a clear improvement in awareness levels regarding menstrual cramps among teenage girls who participated in the drama-based health education sessions.

title: Healthcare workers' perception of community involvement in healthcare services utilization: the mediating role of social media
abstract: Access to healthcare is a basic human right closely linked to the principles of equity, which strive to guarantee that all individuals receive healthcare services, regardless of their background or socioeconomic status. This study, therefore, sought to examine healthcare personnel's perceptions of community involvement in healthcare utilization. A simple random technique was employed to sample 352 respondents from a population of 2927. The cross-sectional survey was conducted using a structured questionnaire with a 5-point Likert scale to elicit responses. The study was anchored on Andersen’s model of health service utilization. Partial least squares Structural Equation Model was used to test the hypotheses. All three hypotheses were found to be statistically significant and positively related. Furthermore, social media mediates the relationship between community involvement and healthcare utilization. It is recommended that social media be employed as a strategic tool to disseminate health information to the public. Moreover, social media should be used as a means of promoting healthcare utilization. The study concludes that community involvement strongly influences how often peop

title: Ethics in educational assessment: emerging issues, controversies, and best practices
abstract: Ethical issues in educational assessment have become increasingly significant as schools and educational authorities seek fairness, accountability, and credibility in evaluation processes. This paper discusses the moral dimensions that guide assessment practices and how unethical conduct can weaken the quality and trustworthiness of educational results. Key issues such as bias, validity, reliability, authenticity, confidentiality, privacy, and the rights of test-takers were discussed. Each issue is explored in relation to its practical implications for teachers, learners, and policymakers. The discussion extends to emerging concerns, such as test preparation and coaching, technology-based assessment, inclusion and diversity, social and emotional learning, as well as high-stakes and standardised testing. The paper draws on recent literature and professional codes to explain how these matters influence the fairness and credibility of assessment practices. It argues that ethical awareness and integrity are essential for educators and evaluators to uphold justice and objectivity in measuring learners’ performance. It was suggested that ethical guidelines and best practices that can sup

title: Educational evaluation in a political context: whose interests are served?
abstract: This paper examines the politicization of educational evaluation in Nigeria and its effects on education quality, governance, and social justice. Educational evaluation, which aims to assess programs, policies, and institutional performance, is often influenced by political interests that determine what is measured, who conducts the evaluation, and how results are used. Policymakers, senior administrators, and politically connected actors tend to benefit from these evaluations, while teachers, learners in rural or under-resourced areas, and low-income communities are frequently excluded. Nigerian case studies from primary, secondary, and tertiary education show how political considerations affect evaluation goals, methods, evaluator selection, data interpretation, and dissemination of results. Politicized evaluation distorts educational priorities, produces inequitable resource allocation, undermines institutional credibility, reduces teacher morale, and limits student learning. These outcomes reinforce social inequalities and weaken the capacity of education to promote fairness and opportunity. The paper argues that evaluation should be transparent, independent, merit-based, and i

title: Generalized anxiety disorder and academic performance of students in abuja, nigeria
abstract: This study examined the relationship between generalized anxiety disorder and academic performance of senior secondary school students in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, Nigeria. The correlational design was adopted for the study. Proportionate and random samplings were adopted to select a sample of 1,106 (530 boys and 576 girls) students from a population of 23,072 of SSS II students of public secondary schools in the area of study. Two instruments namely GADQ and MET were used to collect data. The simple linear and multiple regression statistical tools were also used to test the hypotheses at 0.05 level of significance. Results revealed a negative relationship between generalized anxiety disorder and academic performance of students (F = 1.14; b= -0.071, P= 0.285, > 0.05) but not significant; and sex as an interaction term influenced the relationship between generalized anxiety disorder and academic performance (b = 0.189; P = 0.282, > 0.05), but also not significant. title: Management of personal hygiene in secondary institutions of learning amidst current delta strain of covid-19 in south south nigeria
abstract: This research was carried out to investigate the management of personal hygiene among secondary school students in post Covid-19 Era in South-South geopolitical Zone of Nigeria. The implication of this study was to encourage a good personal hygiene daily routine among secondary school female students so as to forestall onset of diseases that could go a long way to affect their well-being as well as academic performance. Three research questions and three hypotheses guided the study. Six intact classes were selected from a population of eighty-four thousand six hundred and four (84,604) secondary school female students. Using multistage sampling, a total of three hundred and sixty (360) secondary school female students were selected from the six states that make up the South-South Nigeria (60 per state).A causal-comparative design was utilized for the study. The Management of Personal Hygiene Questionnaire (MPHQ), validated by experts which achieved a Cronbach’s alpha of 0.82 was used for data collection. title: Nigerian Universities And The Plethora Of Rankings
abstract: The paper examined some global university rankings and situated the performance of Nigerian universities in the league tables. It also broadly identified the criteria that impacted their performance and expressed opinions on the relevance, and appropriateness of such criteria, in the Nigerian University System as well as the capacity of Nigerian universities to compete in each of the rankings. The Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU), QS World Universities Rankings (QS-WUR), Times Higher Education World Universities Rankings (THE-WUR), Times Higher Education Impact Rankings (THE-IR), Times Higher Education Sub-Saharan African Universities Rankings (THE-SSAUR), Webometric Rankings, US News Universities Rankings, and Nigerian Universities Rankings (NUR), were reviewed. The current performance of the top Nigerian universities in each of the rankings was presented and discussed. No Nigerian university appeared among the top 1000 universities in ARWU, QS-WUR, and Webometric rankings. Measures Nigerian universities can take to improve their performance in the global ranking were also discussed. Suggestions were also made regarding what the ranking agencies need to do to improve

title: Mental Health Challenges, Work Behaviour And Career Development Among Female Teachers In Gboko Local Government Area Of Benue State, Nigeria
abstract: This study investigates the relationship between mental health challenges—specifically anxiety disorders, depression, and stress—and career development among women in the Gboko Local Government Area of Benue State, Nigeria. Utilizing a correlational survey research design, data was collected from a sample of 117 female teachers through a researcher-developed questionnaire, the Mental Health Challenges and Career Development Questionnaire (MHCCDQ). The first section gathered personal information from respondents, while the second section comprised 20 items designed to elicit data on the studied variables, employing a four-point Likert scale for responses. The instrument was validated for both face and content by experts in the Department of Guidance and Counselling at the University of Calabar, achieving a reliability coefficient of .85 using Cronbach Alpha statistics. Pearson's Product Moment Correlation Analysis was employed to analyze the data. The findings reveal a significant relationship between the identified mental health issues and the career development of women in the region, indicating that higher levels of anxiety, depression, and stress adversely affect career progress

title: Perceived Health Disorder And Sport Betting Among University Of Uyo Students In Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria
abstract: This study adopted correlational design to examine the relationship between perceived health disorder and sport betting among University of Uyo students in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. Two research questions were posed which were translated into two null hypotheses. The population for the study consists of all the final year students of which a sample of 220 students were selected via purposive, simple random and accidental sampling techniques in University of Uyo students in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. The instruments titled “Perceived Health Disorder and Sport Betting questionnaire (PHDSBQ)” was developed by the researcher and validated by experts and used for data collection. The reliability of the questionnaire using Alpha Cronbach Method gives an average index of 87. The hypotheses were tested using Pearson Product Moment. Correlation Coefficient at .05 level of significance. The findings of the study revealed that perceived anxiety and depression significantly relate with sports betting behaviors among university students in Uyo Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. It therefore concluded that sports betting behaviors among university students depend on depression and anxiety disorder. Based

title: Perceived Effects Of Floods On Agricultural Production And Food Security In South-South, Nigeria
abstract: The study determined the Perceived Effects of floods on agricultural production and food security in South-South, Nigeria. Specifically, “the study assessed the perceived effects of floods on agricultural production and food security; and the strategies for mitigating the impacts of floods on agricultural production and food security in South-South Nigeria. A descriptive survey research design was adopted and it was carried out in South-South region of Nigeria. A total population of 720 consisting 600 farmers and 120 agricultural extension agents were randomly selected from the region and sampled using accidental sampling technique. Structured questionnaire developed by the researcher was used for data collection. The questionnaire was face validated by two experts from the Department of Agricultural Economics, Faculty of Agriculture, University of Calabar, Calabar. Cronbach alpha reliability method was used to ascertain the internal consistency of the instrument and a reliability coefficient of 0.81 was obtained. Data collection was carried out by the researcher and six research assistants. Descriptive statistics was used for data analysis. The findings revealed sixteen (16) effec

title: The Quality Of Curriculum Implementation In Enhancing Saint Therese Inclusive Non-Violence Secondary Schools Academic Achievement In Misungwi District, Mwanza Tanzania
abstract: The aim of the study was to determine whether or not implementing the newly reformed curriculum was effective in improving academic performance in Saint Therese Inclusive Non-Violence Secondary Schools in Misungwi District, Mwanza, Tanzania. In the survey design, the data were collected using a structured questionnaire. The study sample consist of 344 participants including 320 students, 12 teachers, and 12 administrative staff using purposive in combination with simple random sampling. Purposively sampled administrators and key stakeholders were purposively selected for their roles attributable to policy implementation. In all, 300 students were randomly selected. The research instrument known as Quality of Curriculum Implementation in Enhancing Saint Theresa Inclusive Non-Violence Secondary Schools Questionnaire (QCIESTINSSQ) was administered together with students’ terminal results to measure academic achievement. The consistency of the instrument was confirmed by its reliability (Cronbach's Alpha: 0.71–0.83). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. title: Science Educators' Perspective On The Use Of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Ai) In The Teaching Of Chemistry In Lagos State, Nigeria
abstract: Generative models are artificial intelligence systems that can create humanlike text, pictures, and videos by learning from complex datasets. They use deep learning techniques to understand and replicate the patterns, contents, and structure of language. The research aims to investigate the attitudes, beliefs, and perceptions of science educators in Lagos State regarding the use of Generative AI (GAI) in the teaching of Chemistry. The study adopted a well-structured electronic questionnaire for data collection. Then it was subjected to descriptive and inferential statistics using one-way Analysis of variance (ANOVA). The study revealed no significant difference in Chemistry educators' perception of GAI between educators' gender and teaching experience. This implies that the gender and experiences of the Science educators do not determine the possession of GAI knowledge or enthusiasm to teach it in teaching and learning. In conclusion, 21st-century science educators are more conversant with GAI and are ready to explore its use. title: Influence Of School On Wheel Programme Of Nomadic Education On Pastoralists’ Children School Enrolment And Retention In Gombe State, Nigeria
abstract: The study determined the influence of School on Wheel Programme of Nomadic Education on Pastoralists’ Children School Enrolment and Retention in Gombe State, Nigeria. Two (2) research objectives guided the study. Two (2) research questions were answered and Two (2) hypotheses tested. The population of this study was 80 nomadic primary schools. Out of which 60 were purposively sample, among which were thirty (30), conventional nomadic primary school and thirty (30), nomadic primary school on wheel programme were identified within and outside the boundary of Gombe State. The study adopted ex-post-facto research design. School pro-forma was adopted and used for data collection. The data collected for the study was analyzed using mean, standard deviation and t-test statistic was used to test the null hypotheses at 0.05, level of significance. The findings of the study revealed that; nomadic school on wheel programme had significant influence on the enrolment rate of pastoralists children in Gombe State with a t-value of -4.059 and a p- value of 0.002, school on wheel programme had no significant influence on the retention rate of pastoralists children with t-value of -1.07, p-value 0.2

title: The Role Of Economics Education In Promoting Entrepreneurship: A Study On How Economics Education Influences Entrepreneurial Intentions And Skills In Young Graduates
abstract: Entrepreneurship has emerged as a critical driver of economic development, employment generation, and innovation. In many economies, particularly developing nations, youth unemployment remains a major challenge. Economics education plays a crucial role in shaping entrepreneurial intentions and equipping young graduates with the necessary skills to navigate the business landscape. This study examines how economics education influences entrepreneurial intentions and skills among young graduates, focusing on the theoretical and empirical linkages between economic knowledge and business creation. The study employs the Human Capital Theory, Theory of Planned Behavior, and Entrepreneurial Learning Theory to analyze the impact of economics education on entrepreneurship. Using current literature and empirical studies, this paper highlights the significance of economics education in fostering an entrepreneurial mindset, financial literacy, and risk-taking ability among young graduates. The findings suggest that an effective economics curriculum should integrate entrepreneurship education, practical training, and policy support to enhance graduate employability and business creation. title: Financial Sustainability Of Early Childhood Education Programs: Administrative Insights
abstract: Financial sustainability is a critical challenge in early childhood education (ECE) administration, impacting programme accessibility, quality, and long-term viability. This review examines key financial management strategies, funding models, and budget planning techniques essential for ensuring the stability of ECE programmes. Effective budget planning, including needs assessment, cost-benefit analysis, and contingency planning, are crucial for optimizing financial resources. Various funding models, such as government grants, tuition-based systems, public-private partnerships, and alternative revenue streams, present unique advantages and limitations. Transparent financial reporting, cost-efficiency measures, and revenue diversification are identified as core strategies for maintaining financial resilience. Additionally, financial literacy among ECE administrators plays a pivotal role in sustainable fiscal decision-making, supporting the development of long-term financial plans that align with institutional goals. The paper highlights the need for innovative financing models, such as social impact investing and policy-driven funding interventions, to enhance the financial sustaina

title: Professional Development Opportunities And Job Effectiveness Of Agricultural Educators In University Of Calabar, Cross River State Nigeria
abstract: The relationship between professional development opportunities and job effectiveness of agricultural educators in University of Calabar was determined in this study. Three research questions and hypotheses guided the study. Applying correlation design, the study targeted 16 agricultural educators currently engaged by UNICAL and was all involved in the study. Mixed methods of data collection were employed by the researchers. The quantitative data was collected through a 28-item structured questionnaire while the qualitative data was collected through Focused Group Discussion (FGD). The qualitative data obtained through FGD was used to answer the research questions while Pearson Product Moment Correlation analysis was used to test the hypotheses at 0.05 level of significance. From the data analyzed, agricultural educators agreed that both staff training, conference attendance and use of ICT gadgets are invaluable to their job effectiveness and decried the near absence of these career opportunities at the moment in UNICAL. title: Educational Funding Systems And Quality Service Delivery In University Of Calabar, Calabar, Cross River State, Nigeria
abstract: The study aimed to examine educational funding systems and quality service delivery in the University of Calabar, Calabar, Cross River State, Nigeria. To achieve the aim of this study, two research questions were raised and two hypotheses were formulated to guide the study. A survey research design was adopted for the study. A total sample of 116 Heads of Department in the University of Calabar, Calabar, in Cross River State was selected for the study. The selection was done through the census sampling technique. title: Effect Of Cooperative Learning Strategy On Chemistry Achievement Of Senior Secondary Students In Onueke Education Zone, Ebonyi State
abstract: This study aimed to determine the impact of cooperative learning strategy on students' chemistry achievement and retention in senior secondary schools within the Onueke Education Zone of Ebonyi State. To address this objective, three research questions and hypotheses were formulated. A quasi-experimental, non-equivalent control group design was adopted, involving two groups of students. A multi-stage sampling technique was employed to select a representative sample of 228 SSII chemistry students from six coeducational government-owned senior secondary schools. Initially, the target population of SSII students across 68 schools was stratified. Subsequently, six public secondary schools were simple randomly drawn from these strata. Finally, 3 schools from these six schools were randomly drawn and used as experimental group while the remaining 3 schools used as the control group. This combined sampling approach ensured both representativeness and controlled experimentation.
